book_title: The Book of the Master and the Boy

preface.title: How to Read a Conversation Made of Doors

chapters.title: The Persian Who Was Dead and Revived
chapters.rationale: Opens with the parable of the Persian whose ignorance was lifted, framing the duty to pass on what one has received.

chapters.title: A Stranger in the City
chapters.rationale: The seeker arrives among quarreling theologians, answers their probes, and delivers a public address on the hidden God.

chapters.title: The Boy at the Door — Limits and Conditions
chapters.rationale: One youth follows the Master into private dialogue, establishes the need for a guide, and accepts the binding covenant.

chapters.title: How the World Was Made
chapters.rationale: The Master sets out a cosmology of will-command-saying, the seven origins, pairs, and the corresponding ranks of imams and proofs.

chapters.title: The World, the Hereafter, and the Speech of Parables
chapters.rationale: Dialogue turns from cosmology to the moral status of this world, the doctrine of inner meaning, and the grammar of likeness.

chapters.title: Three Layers of Knowledge
chapters.rationale: A new register: outer law, inner meaning, and the inner-of-inner, the ranks of believers, and the censured scholars of asceticism.

chapters.title: The Five Shares and the Long Road to the Shaykh
chapters.rationale: The boy renounces wealth, his father blesses him, and the Master leads him to the greater Shaykh where he is renamed and initiated.

chapters.title: Homecoming, the Father, and the Debate with Abu Malik
chapters.rationale: The boy reconciles with his father, becomes Salih, and faces Abu Malik's delegation in the climactic theological debate on justice, oneness, and the unbroken line of guides.
